newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan envoy visits C.America to foil HK fallout.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan envoy visits C.America to foil HK fallout.

text.p: Taiwan's top envoy embarked on Wednesday on a tour of central America and the Caribbean to head off possible fallout as rival China used its takeover of Hong Kong to squeeze the island's handful of diplomatic allies.

"I feel I should get in touch with our allies as soon as possible," Foreign Minister John Chang told reporters as he left to visit 11 central American and Caribbean nations that recognise Taipei rather than communist Beijing.
Chang said he would exchange views with his counterparts on post-handover Hong Kong and explain Taipei's policies toward Beijing during his 22-day tour.
"I want to give them a comprehensive understanding (of the China-Taiwan-Hong Kong situation) so that they will give us their full support in the international arena," Chang said.
Beijing, which took over Hong Kong on Tuesday, is forcing nations that maintain formal links with Taiwan to downgrade or even close their Hong Kong consulates.

Beijing has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since the Chinese Nationalists fled there after their 1949 civil war defeat, and sees Hong Kong's return as a model for the island's eventual "reunification with the motherland".
Communist China insists the Nationalist-ruled island is not eligible to join major international organisations and warns other countries not to forge ties with Taiwan or arm it.

Five central American states opened a Taipei trade office on Tuesday and Taiwan reciprocated by kicking in half of a $200 million development fund as the allies closed ranks after Hong Kong's absorption by China.
The office will take over some operations that had been conducted at the five states' Hong Kong consulates.
Chang's visit also aimed to lay the groundwork for President Lee Teng-hui's attendance at a September 7-10 international conference in Panama.
Lee has accepted an invitation to attend a high-level conference for users of the Panama Canal Zone, seen by Taiwan as a rare chance for meetings with world leaders.
Chang's journey will take him to Honduras, El Salvador, Panama, Costa Rica, Belize, the Dominican Republic, St Lucia, Grenada, St Vincent, Dominica and St Christopher.
Most of Taiwan's 30 diplomatic allies are underdeveloped states in Africa and central America.
Taiwan and China have competed aggressively for diplomatic recognition since 1949, often accusing each other of using large sums of cash and aid to woo potential backers.

Beijing launched war games and missile tests to intimidate the island after Lee made a private but high-profile visit to the United States in mid-1995, seen by China as a move to promote Taiwan independence.
